draft.title: Christian bioethics
card: Bioethics asks moral questions about medicine and the start and end of life. Christians often bring two ideas to these questions: the sanctity of life and the dignity of each person.
Human life is a gift from God and is holy. Many Christians draw on the teaching that people are made in the image of God.
Every person has worth that does not depend on age, health or usefulness. This worth is given by God and is not earned.

Churches apply these ideas differently. The Catholic Church opposes euthanasia and IVF that destroys embryos. Some Protestant churches accept IVF more readily, and Christians still debate end-of-life care.
draft.remember: Christians share the sanctity of life and human dignity, but churches may reach different views on euthanasia and IVF.

a.q: Why do many Christians oppose euthanasia?
opts: They see life as a gift from God, so it is holy
They think medicine should never be used near death
They believe suffering is always chosen by God
They hold that a person's worth depends on health
a.why: Many Christians see life as a gift from God, so ending it deliberately seems wrong. The idea that worth depends on health is wrong: dignity does not depend on health or usefulness.
a.clue: Think about where life comes from in Christian belief.

b.q: Two Christian churches in Perth disagree about IVF, yet both say they value the dignity of each person. What best explains this?
opts: They apply the same shared ideas to IVF in different ways
One of the churches has rejected the sanctity of life
Only one of the churches draws on Christian teaching
Dignity has no bearing on questions about IVF
b.why: Churches can share ideas such as dignity but weigh them differently, for example over embryos or the wish to have children. The tempting answer that one church has rejected the sanctity of life is wrong, as the card says both draw on shared ideas.
b.clue: Shared starting ideas do not always lead to the same conclusion.

a.best: They see life as a gift from God, so it is holy

b.best: They apply the same shared ideas to IVF in different ways

problems.detail: 'The Catholic Church opposes ... IVF that destroys embryos' implies it accepts IVF that does not destroy embryos. Catholic teaching (Donum Vitae, Dignitas Personae) opposes IVF in general, because it separates conception from the marital act, as well as because embryos are lost. The line should say the Catholic Church opposes IVF.
The clue 'Shared starting ideas do not always lead to the same conclusion' nearly restates the right option, so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.
The right option is the only one without an absolute or extreme claim ('rejected', 'no bearing', 'Only one'), so it stands out by elimination.

check.summary: The card misstates Catholic teaching by implying the Church opposes only IVF that destroys embryos, when it opposes IVF generally. Question b's clue and wording also give the answer away.

b.q: Two Christian churches in Perth disagree about IVF, yet both say they value the dignity of each person. What best explains this?
opts: They apply the same shared ideas to IVF in different ways
